rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human influence on traits and deeds works by propensity, as shown by differences in receptive and barren ground, rather than as a complete determining cause.
rows.anchor: تأثير النبى الإنسانية في الصفات والأعمال على نحو الاقتضاء دون العلية التامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The innate disposition calls people toward true religion and a balanced way, while created life can also incline them toward corruption without determining it.
rows.anchor: ولا تجامع دعوة الفطرة إلى الدين الحق والسنة المعتدلة دعوة الخلقة إلى الشر والفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects the claim that felicity and misery are essential or fixed by an irrevocable decree and that preaching only establishes proof: such proof would be pointless if outcomes were necessary.
rows.anchor: صحة إقامة الحجة بعينها حجة على عدم كون سعادة السعيد وشقاوة الشقي لازمة ضرورية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human nature stands at a fork between felicity and misery, and education, warning, promise, and command make sense because people can choose either path.
rows.anchor: الإنسان في نفسه على ملتقى خطين ومنشعب طريقين السعادة والشقاوة وفي إمكانه أن يختار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person's deeds and traits also relate to surrounding customs and conditions, which usually incline conduct by propensity and can become nearly unchangeable when traits take root.
rows.anchor: نوع آخر من الارتباط مستقر بين الأعمال والملكات وبين الأوضاع والأحوال والعوامل الخارجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People acquire an initial disposition from bodily constitution and a second character from external influences; neither removes responsibility when its effects arise from prior choices.
rows.anchor: للإنسان شاكلة بعد شاكلة فشاكلة يهيؤها نوع خلقته وخصوصية تركيب بنيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Actions display inward character: arrogance, humility, courage, cowardice, generosity, miserliness, patience, and haste appear across a person's behavior.
rows.anchor: والفعل يمثل فاعله والظاهر عنوان الباطن والصورة دليل المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other verses pair blindness with darkness and the impure with the impure, supporting the principle that deeds correspond to a person's character.
rows.anchor: وما يستوي الأعمى والبصير ولا الظلمات ولا النور ولا الظل ولا الحرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although shākila can be understood in more than one way, the context favors the moral character formed by instincts together with external influences.
rows.anchor: يقرب كون المراد بالشاكلة الشاكلة بالمعنى الثاني وهي الشخصيه الخلقية الحاصلة للإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse answers an objection to the Quran benefiting believers and wrongdoers alike: conduct follows disposition, so a just disposition receives guidance while an unjust one resists it.
rows.anchor: إن أعمالكم تصدر على طبق ما عندكم من الشاكلة والفعلية الموجودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows who has the just character most ready to benefit from truth; Quranic healing and mercy therefore reach believers, while wrongdoers increase in loss unless they abandon injustice.
rows.anchor: والله الذي هو ربكم العليم بسرائركم المدبر لأمركم أعلم بمن عنده شاكلة عادلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparative ‘more guided’ shows that character inclines without compelling: an unjust disposition still retains a weak trace of guidance, while a just one is more receptive.
rows.anchor: الشاكلة الظالمة وإن كانت مضلة داعية إلى العمل الطالح غير أنها لا تحتم الضلال

rows.speaker: الإمام الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī reads the verse as evidence that human souls differ essentially: pure souls receive the Quran as light and perfection, while murky souls receive disgrace and error, like the sun's differing effects on substances.
rows.anchor: وذكر الإمام الرازي في تفسيره ما ملخصه أن الآية تدل على كون النفوس الناطقة الإنسانية مختلفه بالماهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects an essential difference that makes outcomes necessary before habits form; the verse concerns people after character develops through instincts and external factors.
rows.anchor: وأما النفوس الساذجة قبل رسوخ الملكات فلا تختلف بالآثار اختلافا ضروريا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Philosophers argue that an act and its efficient cause share an intrinsic existential relation; otherwise the cause would relate to this act no more than to any other.
rows.anchor: لو لم يكن بين الفعل المعلول وعلته الفاعلة له مناسبة ذاتية وخصوصية واقعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the efficient cause gives existence, it contains the effect's perfection at a higher rank, while the effect represents that cause at a lower rank.
rows.anchor: العلة الفاعلة واجدة لكمال وجود المعلول والمعلول ممثلا لوجودها في مرتبة نازلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mullā Ṣadrā sharpens the account of causation: an effect's very essence is dependence on its cause; otherwise it would first exist independently and cease to be an effect.
rows.anchor: فذاته عين الفقر والتعلق فليس له من الوجود إلا الرابط غير المستقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran treats every thing as a sign of God; created things mirror divine existence and attributes only as dependent signs, not as possessing God's identity.
rows.anchor: الأشياء بما هي مخلوقة له تعالى أفعاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ordinary language spirit is the source of life enabling sensation and voluntary movement; figuratively it can name what gives desired life to souls, such as knowledge.
rows.anchor: الروح على ما يعرف في اللغة هو مبدء الحياة الذي به يقوى الحيوان على الإحساس والحركة الإرادية

rows.speaker: جماعة
rows.claim: Some interpreters take ‘spirit’ figuratively for revelation or the Quran because it gives life to spiritually dead souls, as bodily spirit gives life to bodies.
rows.anchor: لأن به حياة النفوس الميتة كما أن الروح المعروف به حياة الأجساد الميتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Across the Quran's many uses, spirit does not mean the animal life-principle; in some passages it is a distinct being accompanying angels in revelation.
rows.anchor: ولم يرد في جميعها المعنى الذي نجده في الحيوان وهو مبدء الحياة

rows.speaker: علي عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī recalls ʿAlī's argument that the spirit mentioned with angels is distinct from the angels themselves.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم الحديث عن علي عليه السلام أنه احتج بقوله تعالى ينزل الملائكة بالروح من أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel descends with the distinct Spirit, which carries the recited Quran; therefore ‘a spirit from Our command’ in 42:52 means the Spirit's descent, not the Quran itself.
rows.anchor: فجبريل ينزل بالروح والروح يحمل هذا القرآن المقرو المتلو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus is called God's word and a spirit from Him; a created being can be called a divine word, and Jesus was created by the command ‘Be’ without ordinary procreation.
rows.anchor: فعد الروح كلمة دالة على المراد فمن الجائز أن يعد الروح وحيا كما عد كلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ‘from my Lord's command’ identifies spirit as belonging to the kind of divine command, as in other Quranic descriptions of spirit.
rows.anchor: لتبيين الجنس كما في نظائرها من الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's command is His creative ‘Be’: existence considered solely in relation to God, without intermediary causes, time, or place; gradual creation through causes belongs to creation rather than command.
rows.anchor: فالأمر هو وجود الشيء من جهة استناده إليه تعالى وحده والخلق هو ذلك من جهة استناده إليه مع توسط الأسباب الكونية فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one, instantaneous divine command is likened to a blink to deny temporal progression; created processes have a timeless aspect in their direct dependence on God.
rows.anchor: شبه أمره بعد عده واحدة بلمح بالبصر وهذا النوع من التشبيه لنفي التدريج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Embryological stages mediated by causes are distinguished from the human's final creation as another creation, directly attributed to God and thus belonging to command.
rows.anchor: فعد إيجاده المنسوب إلى نفسه من غير تخلل الأسباب الكونية إنشاء خلق آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine command is God's special creative act, above material existence and unmediated by natural causes or temporal and spatial limits.
rows.anchor: الأمر هو كلمة الإيجاد السماوية وفعله تعالى المختص به الذي لا تتوسط فيه الأسباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every thing has a command and a malakut, its more encompassing kingdom; spirit belongs to this elevated, nonmaterial order.
rows.anchor: فقد بان بما مر أن الأمر هو كلمة الإيجاد وهو فعله تعالى الخاص به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran describes several spirits: one with angels, one breathed into humans, one supporting believers, one sent to prophets, and spirit associated with animal and plant life.
rows.anchor: ومنه ما هو منفوخ في الإنسان عامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran sometimes names Spirit separately alongside angels, showing that it is a distinct kind within the spiritual order.
rows.anchor: يوم يقوم الروح والملائكة صفا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some exegetes identify the questioned spirit with the being who stands with angels or ascends with them; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says they offer no proof.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم إن المراد بالروح المسؤول عنه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some identify the spirit as Gabriel because he is called a spirit, but al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects inferring that every use names him; Jesus is also called spirit.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم إن المراد به جبريل فإن الله سماه روحا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the question concerns the Quran and whether it comes from God or Muhammad, with the answer asserting its miraculous divine origin; the author says the name ‘spirit’ elsewhere does not establish that meaning here.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم إن المراد به القرآن لأن الله سماه روحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following verse about removing revelation does not uniquely support the Quran interpretation; it also fits other proposed meanings of spirit.
rows.anchor: على أن الآية التالية لا تتعين تأييدا لهذا الوجه بل تلائم بعض الوجوه الأخر أيضا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take spirit as the human soul and the answer as refusing to disclose its essence; they disagree among themselves whether it is an airy body, bodily part, accident, or the body itself.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم إن المراد به الروح الإنساني فهو المتبادر من إطلاقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects relying on ordinary-language presumption or treating the answer as a ban on inquiry; Quranic verses about spirit disprove these accounts.
rows.anchor: وفيه أن التبادر في كلامه تعالى ممنوع

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the question asks whether spirit is eternal or created, and the answer means it is created by God's act; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī finds no textual basis for this question.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم إن المراد به مطلق الروح الواقع في كلامه والسؤال إنما هو عن كونه قديما أو محدثا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes also disagree whether ‘spirit is from my Lord's command’ answers the question or turns away from it; which reading fits depends on their different identifications of spirit.
rows.anchor: ثم إن لهم اختلافا في معنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context favors addressing the questioners themselves, likely Jews, since they were known for learning; Quraysh and other Arabs are elsewhere called people who do not know.
rows.anchor: والأنسب بالسياق أن يكون الخطاب متوجها إلى السائلين والكلام من تمام قول النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In context the revelation that God could remove is the heavenly Spirit carrying the Quran; no advocate could demand its return or compel God to restore it.
rows.anchor: الروح النازل عليك الملقي بالقرآن إليك من أمرنا غير خارج من قدرتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘revealed’ thing is the divine Spirit sent to the Prophet, as in 42:52; the ‘advocate’ is one who demands its return, not a custodian preserving or reciting the Quran.
rows.anchor: المراد بالوكيل للمطالبة والرد لما أذهبه الله دون الوكيل في حفظ القرآن وتلاوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Except as a mercy’ supplies an ellipsis: the Prophet received and retained the Spirit only by his Lord's mercy, whose favor upon him was great.
rows.anchor: استثناء من محذوف يدل عليه السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓahīr means helper, derived from back; the pronoun in ‘its like’ refers to the Quran, expressed through a noun in place of the pronoun.
rows.anchor: الظهير هو المعين مأخوذ من الظهر كالرئيس من الرأس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge covers every Quranic perfection in wording and meaning, not eloquence alone, since the verse calls all humans and jinn to join forces.
rows.anchor: التحدي بجميع ما للقرآن من صفات الكمال الراجعة إلى لفظه ومعناه لا بفصاحته وبلاغته وحدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge remains in force after the ancient masters of Arabic eloquence have disappeared: the Quran continues to manifest its own inimitability.
rows.anchor: والقرآن باق على إعجازه متحد بنفسه كما كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣarf al-amthāl means repeating and varying examples, shifting from one explanation and style to another.
rows.anchor: تصريف الأمثال ردها وتكرارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An example describes its subject in a way that makes it vivid and intelligible; the Quran used varied examples to clarify truth and prepare people for faith and gratitude.
rows.anchor: والمثل هو وصف المقصود بما يمثله ويقربه من ذهن السامع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun ‘most people’ replaces the expected pronoun ‘most of them,’ perhaps implying that rejection is characteristic of human nature, as in the earlier description of humanity as ungrateful.
rows.anchor: وضع الظاهر موضع المضمر والأصل أكثرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran repeatedly presented examples clarifying truth and inviting faith and gratitude, but most people refused belief and gratitude.
rows.anchor: والمعنى واقسم لقد كررنا للناس في هذا القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vocabulary means to split or forcefully open, an unfailing spring, the midst of something, fragments, face-to-face, gold, and ascent.
rows.anchor: الينبوع العين التي لا ينضب ماؤها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh proposed miraculous signs including a spring in water-scarce Mecca, a garden with streams, fragments of the sky falling, God and angels visibly present, a golden house, ascent to heaven, and a readable book from heaven.
rows.anchor: والآيات تحكي الآيات المعجزة التي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among the remaining demands, Quraysh asked the Prophet to bring God and angels visibly before them, or to rise into heaven and send down a book; the proposed sight of God is inherently impossible.
rows.anchor: أو تأتي بالله والملائكة قبيلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their demands assigned the Prophet divine, unlimited power, including performing what is intrinsically impossible; prophethood instead entails conveying God's warning and glad tidings.
rows.anchor: وفيها ما هو مستحيل بالذات كالإتيان بالله والملائكة قبيلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both ‘human’ and ‘messenger’ are needed in the answer: humanity denies personal power to perform the signs, while messengership denies power delegated by God to create or act at will.
rows.anchor: دخيل في استقامة الجواب عن اقتراحهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some commentators make ‘messenger’ the main predicate and ‘human’ a preface defending human prophets; they read the reply as saying previous messengers likewise only conveyed what God gave them.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعضهم ما محصله أن معتمد الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects that alternative as unsupported by the passage and dependent on an omitted comparison; he also rejects the claim that the proposed syntax is unidiomatic.
rows.anchor: تحميل من غير دليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports that Quraysh asked the Prophet to ask God for the signs cannot override the Quran's explicit account that they demanded the signs from him directly.
rows.anchor: لا يعارض نص الكتاب بخلافه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question ‘Did God send a human messenger?’ represents the idolaters' belief, whether or not they spoke those exact words.
rows.anchor: حكاية حالهم بحسب الاعتقاد وان لم يتكلموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people who rejected guidance were idolaters, including Quraysh and the Arabs generally; their objection concerned belief in a human messenger, as also shown in their reported response to earlier messengers.
rows.anchor: وإنكار النبوة والرسالة مع إثبات الإله من عقائد الوثنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If angels lived earthly material lives, God would send them an angelic messenger from heaven; earthly existence requires divine guidance delivered by heavenly revelation.
rows.anchor: حتى لو أن طائفة من الملائكة سكنوا الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the usual restriction that a messenger must be the same species as recipients is secondary; the verse stresses earthly life and guidance through a heavenly messenger.
rows.anchor: وأما ما أصر عليه المفسرون من تقييد معنى الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human society needs laws beyond reason alone to resolve inevitable disagreements and secure happiness; people therefore need a distinct revelatory faculty embodied in the prophet.
rows.anchor: فلا بد أن يجهز بشعور آخر يتلقى به ما يفيضه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rational proof for prophecy rests on earthly human life and God's care for human guidance; the verse adds that an angel must bring revelation from heaven.
rows.anchor: فإن مقتضى الحياة الأرضية وعناية الله بهداية عبادة أن ينزل إلى بعضهم ملكا من السماء رسولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A human messenger receives God's religion from a descending angel and conveys it to people; only purified individuals can receive the revelation, though its benefit is universal.
rows.anchor: الرسول إنسان ينزل عليه ملك من السماء بدين الله ثم هو يبلغه الناس بأمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording shifts from ‘raise a human messenger’ to ‘send down an angel messenger’ to make the answer sharper and address opponents who objected specifically to a heavenly angelic mission.
rows.anchor: ليكون أولا أحسم للشبهة وأقطع للتوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says Brahmanic, Buddhist, and Sabian traditions may accept human saviors or divine earthly manifestations but resist an angel sent from God to preach exclusive worship of God.
rows.anchor: ففي التصريح برسالة الملك السماوي إلى البشر الأرضي من عند الله النص على كمال المحالفة لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's gift is not withheld, though only some are prepared to receive revelation; this supports reports from the Imams distinguishing a messenger, who sees and hears the angel, from a prophet, who sees dreams.
rows.anchor: فالفيض عام وإن كان المستفيض خاصا

rows.speaker: أئمه أهل البيت
rows.claim: Reports from the Imams distinguish a messenger, who sees and hears the angel, from a prophet, who sees the angel in dreams but does not encounter him directly.
rows.anchor: الرسول هو الذي يرى الملك ويسمع منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about angels walking securely on earth is a concise image of material earthly life, whose clearest features are spatial movement and terrestrial gravity.
rows.anchor: فإن الانتقال المكاني على الأرض مع الوقوع تحت الجاذبة الأرضية من أوضح خواص الحياة المادية الأرضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the Quranic challenge and their obstinate, baseless demands, God tells the Prophet to end the dispute: he delivered the message and the opponents heard it, so judgment is left to God.
rows.anchor: فقد بلغ ما أرسل به ودعا واحتج وأعذر وقد سمعوا وتمت عليهم الحجة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes God as witness to the truth of the mission, with the Quran itself proving it; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says ‘between me and you’ and ‘knowing and seeing His servants’ do not fit that reading well.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالآية الاستشهاد بالله سبحانه على حقية الدعوة وصحة الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These three successive verses end with the same rhyme on rasūlā, a unique sequence of three consecutive Quranic verses sharing this rhyme.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية والآيتان قبلها مسجعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guidance and misguidance statement continues the Prophet's final command to stop disputing; it is not a new, independent passage outside the command to say it.
rows.anchor: إن الآية كلام مبتدأ غير داخل في حيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone guides; those He leaves astray have no helpers to guide them, so the Prophet should stop hoping that these opponents will believe.
rows.anchor: فمن هداه فهو المهتدي لا غير ومن أضله ولم يهده فلن تجد يا محمد له أولياء من دونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural ‘helpers’ hints that any supposed protectors would include either numerous idols or the many natural causes people rely on.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أنه لو كان له ولي من دون الله لكان ذلك إما آلهتهم وهي كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from first-person plural to third person avoids implying that angels share God's authority to guide or misguide, which could suggest a contradiction about their role as alleged gods.
rows.anchor: فقد كان السياق سياق التكلم بالغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing description says the condemned are gathered face-down, blind, mute, and deaf; when Hell's blaze subsides, its flames are increased again.
rows.anchor: وخبو النار وخبوها سكون لهبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first creation proves God's power to create a comparable body again; the person's identity is preserved by the soul, which remains with God despite the body's decay.
rows.anchor: ملاك الوحدة والشخصية هي النفس الإنسانية وهي محفوظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 32:10–11, the Angel of Death answers the objection that the person vanished: he takes the person whole, while only the body is lost and later remade.
rows.anchor: فأجيب عنه بأن ملك الموت يتوفى الإنسان ويأخذه تاما كاملا فلا يضل ولا يتلاشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All verses about return to God, resurrection, questioning, judgment, and recompense show the resurrected person is the same individual; body-only comparison follows the objectors' focus on bodily remains.
rows.anchor: والدليل على أن الإنسان المبعوث هو عين الإنسان الدنيوي لا مثله جميع آيات القيامة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpret ‘a like of them’ idiomatically as the people themselves; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the wording more likely denies an act by denying its cause or defining quality, which is more emphatic.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن المراد بمثلهم نفسهم فهو من قبيل قولهم مثلك لا يفعل هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appointed term most likely means death, whether the full bounded lifetime or its final moment; reminding deniers of certain death should restrain their defiance.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن المراد بالأجل هو زمان الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī prefers the appointed term as death; taking it as Judgment Day does not suit a context that first records denial of resurrection and then proves God's power.
rows.anchor: وجوز بعضهم أن يكون المراد بالأجل هو يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects as pointless the claim that the term is a second proof of resurrection on either interpretation, calling it an unnecessary strained reading.
rows.anchor: وهو تكلف لا يعود إلى جدوى البتة فلا موجب للاشتغال به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qatūr means extremely stingy; al-Majmaʿ glosses the root as restricting or estimating expenditure, and the verse rebukes those who reject human messengers by imagining themselves owners of divine mercy's stores.
rows.anchor: فسر القتور بالبخيل المبالغ في الإمساك

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report in al-ʿAyyāshī says healing lies in Quranic knowledge, citing the verse that calls the Quran healing and mercy.
rows.anchor: عن مسعدة بن صدقة عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال إنما الشفاء في علم القرآن

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report in al-Kāfī says intention is better than action and is itself action, then reads acting according to one's disposition as acting according to one's intention.
rows.anchor: عن سفيان بن عيينة عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال قال النية أفضل من العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī explains ‘intention is action’ as unity between an act's title and its actual referent.
rows.anchor: وقوله إن النية هي العمل يشير إلى اتحادهما اتحاد العنوان ومعنونه

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report says the people of Hell and Paradise remain there because, in life, they intended to persist forever in disobedience or obedience; it explains disposition as intention, and al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says traits become so rooted that their opposite potential disappears.
rows.anchor: إنما خلد أهل النار في النار لأن نياتهم كانت في الدنيا أن لو خلدوا فيها أن يعصوا الله أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eternal-destiny report indicates that dispositions can become so deeply rooted that the soul loses readiness for the opposite character.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى رسوخ الملكات بحيث يبطل في النفس استعداد ما يقابلها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report says Quraysh asked Jews for a question to pose to Muhammad; they suggested asking about spirit, and the reply led them to cite the Torah before revelation about the sea as ink for God's words.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال قالت قريش لليهود أعطونا شيئا نسأل هذا الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reports place the question among Jews in Medina, but al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says that conflicts with the sura's Meccan setting and unified context.
rows.anchor: وكون السورة مكية واتحاد سياق آياتها لا يلائم ذلك

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī and other compilers transmit ʿAlī's account of a many-faced, many-tongued angel called Spirit; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects it because Quranic usage distinguishes Spirit from angels.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report making Spirit an angel conflicts with Quranic passages that place Spirit alongside angels; an earlier report from ʿAlī likewise argues against identifying them.
rows.anchor: كون الروح من الملائكة لا يوافق ظاهر عدة من آيات الكتاب

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report in al-Kāfī calls Spirit a creation greater than Gabriel and Michael, accompanying Muhammad and the Imams and belonging to the malakut; the author says this agrees with his reading.
rows.anchor: قال خلق أعظم من جبرائيل وميكائيل كان مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding report accords with the Quranic account of Spirit as an order-of-command being with multiple levels.
rows.anchor: والرواية توافق ما تقدم توضيحه من مدلول الآيات

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله عليهما السلام
rows.claim: A report says Spirit is a created being with sight, power, and support that God places in the hearts of prophets and believers; its opening denies that God has an interior or hollow core.
rows.anchor: قال إن الله تبارك وتعالى أحد صمد والصمد الشيء الذي ليس له جوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report's opening guards against taking ‘I breathed into him of My spirit’ to mean God has a cavity or a portion of Himself that was breathed out.
rows.anchor: دفعا لما يتوهم من مثل قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: أحدهما عليهما السلام
rows.claim: A report identifies the spirit in animals and people as coming from the malakut and divine power; the author says it supports a broad, multi-level account and implies animal spirit is immaterial.
rows.anchor: التي في الدواب والناس قلت وما هي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report recounts Quraysh leaders meeting Muhammad at the Kaaba after sunset to argue and excuse their opposition, accusing him of insulting ancestors, attacking religion, dividing the community, and cursing their gods; they offer wealth, leadership, kingship, or medical help if he seeks them or suffers from a jinn.
rows.anchor: اجتمعوا بعد غروب الشمس عند ظهر الكعبة فقال بعضهم لبعض ابعثوا إلى محمد وكلموه وخاصموه
